name: Dumbbell Forearm Pronation

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: AAOS Wrist and Forearm Conditioning Program

steps: Sit with your elbow bent at 90 degrees and your forearm resting flat on a table, holding a light dumbbell or hammer upright.
Hold the dumbbell near the bottom of the handle to create an asymmetric rotational lever arm.
Start with the weight upright and your thumb pointing to the ceiling.
Slowly rotate your forearm inward so your palm turns to face downward toward the table.
Pause for 1 second in full pronation, feeling the pronator muscles on the inside of your forearm.
Slowly rotate your forearm back to the vertical starting position.
coaching_cues: Keep your elbow tucked against your side or anchored on the table; do not swing your shoulder.
Use a light weight; rotational torque increases significantly with a long lever arm.
Maintain smooth, controlled speed throughout the rotation.

sources.attribution: AAOS Wrist and Forearm Conditioning Program
